Subject: Clarify billing for our long-context use

Ben —

Quick question as we finalize the SOW: our R&D team will be sending long clinical notes (up to ~40k tokens) into a single inference call for summarization + redaction. We need clarity on how Redwood will account for billing when: 

- one call includes multiple internal segments (prefixes) that would, under current docs, each trigger the minimum bucket
- we batch server-side vs. client-side to reduce per-token costs
- rounding occurs (do you always round up to the next 1k token quantum or do you have a per-call floor)

Can you confirm whether there is a way to avoid double-charging for duplicated prefixes and whether there are proration rules for monthly packs when usage hits these long calls?

Thanks,
Jamie

Jamie — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: we have a few levers to prevent what you're describing (double-billing on repeated prefixes and unnecessary quantum rounding). Longer answer below and attached is an updated pricing summary (redwood_pricing_v2.pdf). Key points:

1) Prefix deduplication within a single request: our runtime does prefix/KV dedupe at the request edge for identical byte sequences. If your pipeline sends identical context blocks in one API call, we will not charge those tokens twice. That covers the duplication case inside a single call.

2) Cross-call prefix reuse (persistent KV): we give persistent KV reuse credits for repeated prefixes across calls when pinned to the same session id. For enterprise customers on Dedicated/Dedicated-Reserve we can increase the retention window for KV reuse — that shows up as a straightforward offset on the invoice rather than a separate line item.

3) Quantum and rounding: default hosted meter rounds usage at the 100-token quantum for small calls and 1k-token quantum for very large models; however, for negotiated packs (monthly prepay / slab) we can change the consumption granularity to avoid large upward rounding. For your deal size I propose using a blended quantum of 250 tokens to keep rounding noise low while preserving billing simplicity.

4) Long single-call handling: when a single request exceeds the context-cap for a model and is split by the runtime, we bill the actual tokenization after internal stitching (we do not charge per logical split). This means your 40k-token single logical call will be charged based on the tokenized content post-compaction, with an applied per-call floor only if the call is below the floor threshold.

5) Proration and monthly packs: for monthly prepay slabs, we prorate leftover micro-credits on true-ups (not rounded credits). If a long call would normally push you over the slab in a single day, we'll surface a one-time overage invoice line with the negotiated overage rate rather than forcibly consuming an extra slab increment.

Next steps I'd propose:
- I can run a short invoice-sensitivity calc using a sample 40k token payload you provide (takes me ~1 hour).
- If you'd like, we can include a clause in the SOW that defines "prefix equivalence" (hash algorithm + session id) and the proration method for monthly slabs.

Attaching redwood_pricing_v2.pdf and a draft MOP doc for your internal counsel.

- Grace: if we add a "prefix equivalence" clause to the SOW that references a SHA256-based hash + session-id, is that standard/legally reasonable? Acme wants it explicit so their auditors don't flag double-billing.
